extra-.et: From Latin extra (“outside, except, beyond”, adverb and preposition), from exter (“being on the outside”).

s: separate (not included in or directly connected to the object being discussed)
Das is’n ganz extra Rezept von meiner Mutter.
This is a very special recipe of my mother’s.
extra.et: Borrowed from Latin extrā, see also the similarly borrowed prefix extra-. Pfeifer speculates that the standalone usage with the sense of "separate" arises out of phrases like extrā ōrdinem (“out of the ordinary”) which occurs in 16th century German chancellary…

s: Das Wrack wurde mit extra entworfenen Bergungskränen gehoben.
The wreck was lifted with specifically designed salvage cranes.
Das hab ich doch nich’ extra gemacht!
I didn't do that on purpose!
Können Sie mir die Fritten und die Wurst extra abpacken?
Could you wrap the fries and the sausage separately?
Vorsicht! Der Tee is’ extra heiß!
Be careful! The tea is extra hot!
